senses.definition: (onomatopoeia) A sound mimicking the loss of air, as if someone's solar plexus had just been struck.

quotes.text: Whap, Biff, Ooooof, Sock, Pow, Zok! Batman is back. Gotham City is again leaving its law and order in the hands of a man who wears plastic underpants over his tights.

senses.definition: (slang) Synonym of ouch (“expressing sympathy at another's pain, shock at a high price, etc.”).

quotes.text: "Oof, you just lost a lot of progress. That's a real frustration, a real punch in the gut."

senses.definition: A sound made in pain, as when expelling air after being struck.

quotes.text: The soldier on the ground clutched his head and then his stomach and gave an "oof" of pain.

senses.definition: (Internet slang) Something cringeworthy, or which arouses disappointment; often used in conjunction with the qualifier big.

quotes.text: Fans were quick to express their disappointment at the removal of what has now become an iconic sound in the gaming space. The audio is trending on Twitter under #SaveTheOOF and Big Oof.

examples: What's he after? Oof—oof—oof, that's what he's after. He's for his own pocket, he's for being boss of all the woolly West. He's after keeping us poor and making himself rich.

quotes.text:
Burlington Bertie's the latest young jay
He rents a swell flat somewhere Kensington way
He spends the good oof that his pater has made
Along with the Brandy and Soda Brigade.
Chuffy: It's on a knife edge at the moment, Bertie. If he can get planning permission, old Stoker's going to take this heap off my hands in return for vast amounts of oof.
